query: What in an incident's description tends to signal it's a hardware problem?

per_column.name: affected_system_domain
per_column.rationale: Well-separated, human-readable categories (software_application, hardware_device, database, network_infrastructure, etc.) that can be segmented against hardware_incident. Highly informative for exploring what signals a hardware problem, since 'hardware_device' directly contrasts with other domains. Note: partial overlap with the focus concept, but it is a broader categorical axis rather than a pure restatement.

per_column.name: software_keyword_present
per_column.rationale: Clean binary categories with a reasonable split (351/249). Interpretable and groupable: presence of software terminology is an associational signal that inversely relates to hardware incidents. Somewhat mechanical (keyword flag), but the categories are meaningful and well-separated.

per_column.name: description_action_type
per_column.rationale: Interpretable, well-separated action categories (failure_malfunction, installation_request, connectivity_issue, access_recovery, etc.) derived from the description. These are external associational segments that let an explorer compare which action types co-occur with hardware incidents. Minor NULLs but categories remain meaningful.

judge.rationale: All three columns provide interpretable, well-separated categorical segmentations that can be grouped and compared against the hardware_incident focus, directly serving the query about description signals of hardware problems. affected_system_domain and description_action_type offer rich multi-category axes, while software_keyword_present gives a clean contrastive binary. None are opaque scores or near-constant, and none are pure restatements of the focus (affected_system_domain overlaps but adds a broader domain taxonomy). The set robustly supports discovering interpretable relationships; slight deduction because software_keyword_present is somewhat mechanical and affected_system_domain partially encodes the target concept.
